description: Layered target architecture for the UK commercial bank. Four horizontal layers from customer interaction surface (L1) down to shared platform infrastructure (L4). Each layer is a deployment boundary: services in a lower layer must be available before the layer above can operate. This document is the primary reference for the Step 5 Discovery architecture and feeds directly into the service catalogue and service-dependency build order.

L1.name: Channel Layer
L1.purpose: Customer and partner interaction surfaces — every channel through which a persona initiates a transaction or receives a response. The Channel Layer owns no business logic; it delegates immediately to the Capability Layer via the API Gateway (SVC-101). Channels are stateless presentation concerns: session state lives in IAM (SVC-100); business state lives in domain services.

components.name: Web Portal
components.description: Browser-based online banking for personal and business customers. Authenticated via SCA-compliant session (SVC-100). Reaches Retail Banking Core (SVC-001), Commercial Banking Core (SVC-005), and Digital Channels (SVC-017).
components.technology_notes: React SPA. WCAG 2.1 AA mandatory. Deployed to CDN with UK-only data residency for session tokens.

components.name: Mobile App
components.description: Native iOS and Android application for personal and business customers. Primary interaction surface — 70%+ of digital sessions. Biometric SCA, real-time push notifications, in-app card controls.
components.technology_notes: React Native or Swift/Kotlin native. APNS/FCM push via Notification Service (SVC-053). Deep-link scheme for Open Banking consent journeys.

components.name: Open Banking API
components.description: OBIE-compliant AISP/PISP API surface for FCA-registered Third Party Providers. FAPI 1.0 Advanced profile. Rate-limited via API Gateway. Covers Account Information, Payment Initiation, and Variable Recurring Payments.
components.auth_model: FAPI 1.0 Advanced (eIDAS/OBIE certificate + PKCE). TPP certificates validated by SVC-101.
components.technology_notes: OpenAPI 3.0. OBIE Read/Write API v3.1.x. Consent managed by Digital Channels Service (SVC-017). Hosted at api.bank.co.uk/open-banking.

components.name: Branch Terminal
components.description: In-branch staff workstation providing identity-verified account opening, cash transactions, complaint logging, and referral workflows. Authenticated via bank employee SSO. Reaches Internal Portal backend services.
components.auth_model: SAML 2.0 SSO (employee directory) + hardware token MFA
components.technology_notes: Browser-based internal app. Thin-client model. All branch terminals route through the internal network; no direct internet exposure.

components.name: SWIFT Network
components.description: Bank's direct SWIFT participant interface for CBPR+ ISO 20022 cross-border payment messaging and correspondent banking. Used by treasury dealers and correspondent banks. SWIFT Alliance Access / SAA Cloud gateway.
components.auth_model: SWIFT PKI (HSM-backed BIC certificate). No OAuth — SWIFT is a closed network.
components.technology_notes: ISO 20022 MX mandatory since November 2025. Connected to International Payments Service (SVC-010). SAA Cloud reduces on-premises SWIFT hardware obligation.

components.name: Internal Portal
components.description: Staff-facing portal aggregating CRM, RM workflow (Commercial Banking), wealth advisory tools (Wealth Platform), compliance monitoring dashboards, and payment operations exception queues. All internal personas access banking systems through this surface.
components.auth_model: SAML 2.0 SSO + hardware MFA. SM&CR role-based access enforced by IAM (SVC-100).
components.technology_notes: Micro-frontend architecture over internal API Gateway. Role-based routing to domain service dashboards. Privileged access sessions logged to Audit & Logging (SVC-103).

components.name: Regulatory Gateway
components.description: Secure file transfer channel for regulatory submissions to FCA, PRA, HMRC, and Bank of England. Delivers COREP, FINREP, PRA 110, and CHAPS ISO 20022 enhanced data submissions. Outbound-only from the bank's perspective.
components.auth_model: HMRC/FCA/PRA regulator portal credentials. SFTP or direct API submission (FCA DRR direction).
components.technology_notes: Managed by Compliance Core Service (SVC-015). AxiomSL or equivalent regulatory reporting platform generates submission artefacts. Immutable log of all submissions in Audit & Logging (SVC-103).

components.name: Card Network Interface
components.description: Real-time card scheme connectivity for debit card and commercial card authorisation, clearing, and settlement via Visa and Mastercard networks. Serves both issuing (SVC-011) and acquiring (SVC-008) functions.
components.auth_model: Visa/Mastercard scheme TLS with hardware BIN authentication. PCI DSS CDE boundary enforced at this channel.
components.technology_notes: Managed by Card Processing Service (SVC-011) via Marqeta/Thredd bureau. Sub-100ms authorisation SLA. PCI DSS v4.0 scoped.

components.name: Telephony
components.description: Telephone banking channel for customers and a contact point for branch staff. Provides IVR for balance enquiry and payment initiation, escalation to human agents for complex queries. Biometric voice authentication for high-value transactions.
components.auth_model: IVR PIN + knowledge-based authentication. Biometric voice print for repeat callers.
components.technology_notes: Integrated with Notification Service (SVC-053) for outbound fraud alerts. Customer data retrieved from Retail Banking Core (SVC-001) and Commercial Banking Core (SVC-005) via Internal Portal APIs.

components.name: Corporate API
components.description: Host-to-host API channel for corporate treasury clients integrating their ERP systems (SAP, Oracle) directly with the bank's payment and cash management infrastructure. REST/OpenAPI with bulk payment file submission and real-time balance feeds.
components.auth_model: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials + mTLS client certificate. Dedicated rate limits per corporate client.
components.technology_notes: Hosted at api.bank.co.uk/corporate. Connected to Commercial Banking Core (SVC-005), Domestic Payments (SVC-009), International Payments (SVC-010), and Treasury Service (SVC-007) via API Gateway (SVC-101).

L2.name: Capability Layer
L2.purpose: Domain services — the runtime deployment layer for all 17 banking domain services and 6 cross-cutting shared services. Each service owns a bounded data domain, publishes well-defined event contracts, and has a single owning capability. Services in this layer depend on the Cross-Cutting Services Layer (L3) and the Platform Layer (L4) but do not depend on other L2 services synchronously except where documented as hard_blocking. The Capability Layer is the source of all regulated business logic and the unit of PRA/FCA important business service decomposition.

L3.name: Cross-Cutting Services Layer
L3.purpose: Six shared infrastructure services consumed by multiple domain services. These are not business capability services — they resolve shared sub-capabilities that appear across multiple domains (see shared-sub-capabilities.json). They are owned by the domain with the strongest regulatory accountability for that concern, but consumed bank-wide. They sit between the Capability Layer (L2) and the Platform Layer (L4) because they depend on platform services but are consumed by domain services.

components.name: Customer Onboarding Service
components.pattern: Resolves SSC-001. Single KYC clearance gate before any account provisioning.

components.name: Sanctions Screening Service
components.pattern: Resolves SSC-002. Hard blocking dependency on all payment execution paths.

components.name: Credit Decision Service
components.pattern: Resolves SSC-003. Versioned credit model API. PRA IRB model accountability.

components.name: Notification Service
components.pattern: Event-driven. Subscribes to domain events from all capabilities. Manages GDPR consent state.

components.name: Document Management Service
components.owned_by: CAP-002 (Commercial Banking / Trade Finance document aspect)
components.pattern: Resolves SSC-004. ETDA 2023 compliant. Regulatory retention enforcement.

components.name: Workflow Engine
components.pattern: Durable workflow orchestration for long-running multi-step processes. SM&CR approval chains.

L4.name: Platform Layer
L4.purpose: Seven foundation services providing the shared infrastructure that all capabilities depend on. These services have no capability_mapping to a business capability — they are platform concerns owned by the Platform / CTO function. All are strong-buy: the bank does not build competitive advantage in foundational infrastructure. Platform services are T0 or T2 by tier and must be operational before any domain service is deployed.

components.name: Identity & Access Management
components.description: Authentication, authorisation, SCA compliance, TPP certificate validation, SSO, RBAC/ABAC, SM&CR role assignments.

components.name: API Gateway
components.description: External and internal API management, rate limiting, TLS termination, Open Banking FAPI compliance, developer portal, usage analytics.

components.name: Event Bus
components.description: Durable event streaming (Kafka/Confluent), schema registry, pub-sub delivery, dead letter queues. Primary integration mechanism between domain services.

components.name: Audit & Logging
components.description: Immutable audit log, SIEM, structured log aggregation, 5-7 year retention enforcement. Foundation for all regulatory evidence and SM&CR accountability.

components.name: Data Platform
components.description: Enterprise data lake and warehouse, feature store for ML models, data catalogue with lineage, regulatory reporting data aggregation, Consumer Duty analytics.

components.name: Secrets Management
components.description: HSM-backed key storage, automatic secrets rotation, dynamic credentials, PCI DSS key management, GDPR encryption key lifecycle.

components.name: Service Mesh
components.description: mTLS service-to-service encryption, traffic management, circuit breaking, distributed tracing, zero-trust deny-all baseline policy. PCI DSS network segmentation evidence.

observability_and_security_services.description: Seven additional services introduced in Step 5 to complete the observability pipeline and enforce the zero-trust security posture. These services span T0-T3 tiers and are documented fully in service-dependencies.json.

services.name: OTel Collector
services.description: OpenTelemetry Collector sidecar/gateway. Collects, processes, and routes traces, metrics, and logs from all services to the observability stores. Zero-config instrumentation for all containerised services.

services.name: Log Store
services.description: Centralised structured log storage (Elasticsearch / OpenSearch). Receives log streams from SVC-107. Query interface for incident investigation and FCA supervisory data requests.

services.name: Trace Store
services.description: Distributed trace storage (Jaeger / Tempo). Receives traces from SVC-107. Enables end-to-end latency analysis and root-cause tracing across service boundaries for important business service impact tolerance monitoring.

services.name: Metrics Store
services.description: Time-series metrics storage (Prometheus / Thanos). Receives metrics from SVC-107. Feeds SVC-112 Observability Aggregator for SLA alerting and PRA operational resilience reporting.

services.name: Audit Log Store (WORM)
services.description: Write-Once Read-Many immutable audit log store for regulatory-grade tamper-evident records. Receives from SVC-103. Minimum 7-year retention enforced (PRA financial records). Separate from general log store to prevent audit record commingling.

services.name: Observability Aggregator
services.description: Dashboards, alerting, SLA monitoring, and operational reporting aggregating from SVC-108/109/110. Single pane-of-glass for IT Operations (PER-060). Feeds FCA operational resilience impact tolerance monitoring.

services.name: Zero-Trust Policy Engine
services.description: Centralised policy decision point (OPA / Styra) for zero-trust authorisation assertions across all services. Evaluates access policies referencing IAM attributes (SVC-100), service mesh identity (SVC-106), and risk signals from SVC-013. Enables declarative policy-as-code for SM&CR access governance.

layer_relationships.description: All channels invoke domain services via SVC-101 (API Gateway) using REST/OpenAPI or event publication. No channel has direct database access to any domain service.
layer_relationships.protocol: HTTPS/TLS 1.3. Open Banking channels use FAPI 1.0. Corporate API uses mTLS + OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials.

layer_relationships.description: Domain-to-domain integration uses the Event Bus (SVC-102) for async flows and direct synchronous API calls for hard blocking dependencies (e.g. SVC-009 → SVC-051 for sanctions screening). Cross-domain synchronous calls are minimised: the target pattern is event-driven with compensating sagas for cross-service transactions.
layer_relationships.protocol: gRPC for high-throughput real-time paths (fraud, sanctions, card authorisation). REST/OpenAPI for all other inter-service calls.

layer_relationships.description: Domain services call cross-cutting services for shared concerns. Pattern: share contracts not implementations. Cross-cutting services publish events back to the event bus on completion (e.g. KYCClearanceGranted, SanctionsCleared).
layer_relationships.protocol: REST/OpenAPI (SVC-050, SVC-052, SVC-053, SVC-054, SVC-055). gRPC for SVC-051 sanctions screening (sub-200ms SLA in payment path).

layer_relationships.description: All domain and cross-cutting services consume platform services as infrastructure: IAM for authentication, API Gateway at the edge, Event Bus for pub-sub, Audit & Logging for all regulated events, Secrets Management for credentials, Service Mesh for service-to-service security.
layer_relationships.protocol: Platform services are infrastructure — not application-level calls. Service Mesh is a sidecar; Secrets are injected at startup; IAM tokens are validated by API Gateway before requests reach domain services.

layer_relationships.description: Cross-cutting services consume platform services identically to domain services. SVC-050 depends on SVC-102 (Event Bus) to publish KYC events; SVC-051 depends on SVC-103 for immutable sanctions screening records.

Within the platform layer, SVC-101 (API Gateway) depends on SVC-100 (IAM) for token validation. SVC-105 (Secrets Management) depends on SVC-100 for machine identity. SVC-106 (Service Mesh) depends on SVC-100 for SPIFFE/SPIRE certificate coordination. SVC-104 (Data Platform) depends on SVC-102 (Event Bus) for streaming ingestion.
layer_relationships.protocol: Internal platform service calls. Not exposed to higher layers.

design_decisions.decision: The Channel Layer (L1) is stateless. All session state is held in the IAM platform (SVC-100); all financial state is held in domain services (L2). Channels are CDN-deployable, horizontally scalable, and have no local data stores.
design_decisions.rationale: Stateless channels allow independent horizontal scaling during peak load (e.g. Black Friday, bank rate announcement) without scaling domain services. FCA operational resilience requires demonstrable recovery within impact tolerance windows — stateless channels are the fastest to recover as there is no state to restore.
alternatives_considered: Session state in channel application servers
design_decisions.rejected_because: Sticky sessions create single-point-of-failure risk during horizontal scaling events and make the channel layer a stateful component that must be included in the bank's important business service recovery planning.

design_decisions.decision: Event Bus (SVC-102) is the primary integration mechanism between domain services. Synchronous cross-domain API calls are permitted only for hard blocking regulatory dependencies (sanctions screening in the payment path; KYC clearance at onboarding).
design_decisions.rationale: An event-driven architecture provides loose coupling, independent deployability, and a durable audit trail of all domain events for regulatory replay (PRA supervisory investigation). The number of synchronous cross-domain calls is minimised to prevent cascading availability failures where one domain service's downtime propagates to all its synchronous callers.
alternatives_considered: Synchronous REST for all inter-service communication
design_decisions.rejected_because: Synchronous REST creates tight coupling and cascading failure risk. A mid-tier bank's important business services (payments, digital banking) cannot afford cascading failures — the event-driven pattern with async compensation is the standard architecture for resilient financial systems at this scale.

design_decisions.decision: gRPC is used for high-throughput real-time paths: SVC-013 (Fraud Detection, sub-100ms), SVC-051 (Sanctions Screening, sub-200ms), and SVC-011 (Card Processing, sub-100ms). All other service interfaces use REST/OpenAPI.
design_decisions.rationale: Card authorisation, payment fraud screening, and sanctions screening are in the synchronous blocking path of every payment transaction. At millions of transactions per day, REST over HTTPS adds 10-30ms of serialisation overhead vs gRPC's binary protobuf encoding. gRPC also provides native bidirectional streaming for real-time fraud signal aggregation. The latency savings are material for the bank's payment SLA and APP fraud reimbursement obligations.
design_decisions.rejected_because: REST serialisation overhead is not acceptable on the sub-100ms payment authorisation path. GraphQL adds a query resolution layer that introduces latency and complexity without benefit on high-throughput binary paths.

design_decisions.decision: The Service Mesh (SVC-106) enforces a deny-all baseline with explicit allow-list for all service-to-service communication. PCI DSS CDE-scoped services (SVC-003, SVC-008, SVC-011) are isolated in a separate network segment enforced by service mesh policy.
design_decisions.rationale: PCI DSS v4.0 requires demonstrable network segmentation between the cardholder data environment and non-CDE systems. The service mesh allow-list provides this segmentation at the application network layer with cryptographic evidence (mTLS) for PCI DSS audit. FCA operational resilience mapping also benefits from the service mesh's authoritative service dependency graph.
design_decisions.rejected_because: VLANs and firewall rules are coarse-grained and do not provide per-service identity (SPIFFE). PCI DSS auditors increasingly require application-layer evidence of segmentation in cloud-native environments. Service mesh policy-as-code is the cloud-native standard.

design_decisions.decision: The seven observability and security services (SVC-107 through SVC-113) are first-class architectural components with assigned tiers. Observability is not an afterthought — OTel Collector (SVC-107) is T0, deployed alongside the first platform services.
design_decisions.rationale: FCA PS21/3 operational resilience requires banks to demonstrate they can detect, respond, and recover from disruption to important business services within defined impact tolerances. Without observability infrastructure deployed from Day 1, the bank cannot evidence impact tolerance compliance. Deploying observability at T0 also enables regulatory audit from the first transaction.
alternatives_considered: Deploy observability after domain services are live
design_decisions.rejected_because: Deploying observability post-go-live creates a window of unobservable operation. Vendor-managed observability (Datadog) can receive telemetry but the bank must ensure UK data residency for logs containing personal data — a managed UK-hosted observability stack is required for GDPR compliance.
